benchmark.summary: Frozen held-out evaluation on 6 open-access articles with deposited data (86 true statements, 41 false ones including planted errors, 67 numbers that cannot be derived from the table). Every proposer feeds the same verifier.

arms.label: Gemini, filtered by Nemotron as critic
Nemotron, filtered by Gemini as critic

benchmark.notes: Counts are printed numbers, over original, planted-error and prompt-injection copies of the held-out articles. Rows that cover fewer copies cannot be compared with rows that cover more. “Wrongly” columns include every result on a number that had no gold label, before any hand adjudication. Gold labels are AI-assisted annotations, not expert review. In this evaluation a proved match was reliable when the proposer had not seen the data, and a refutation was often a wrong reading of the sentence, so read “refuted” as “this reading does not hold for this file”. The full report, receipts and replay instructions are in the PCS core repository under research/claimcheck_v1. Adversarial suite: 409 deceptive proposals, 0 accepted; coincidence search submitted 214 numerically matching readings for 62 false or underivable numbers, 3 were proved.

kernel_runner.accepts: only proof files whose generated part is exactly in the generator's form; anything else is refused before Lean is started

withdrawn_runners.reason: it accepted proof files whose generated part had been written by hand, including one that defined its own `run`, so its reports do not show that the reviewed checker was used

kernel_run_meaning.establishes: the supplied mathematical obligation: each theorem in the proof file, about the reviewed checker, holds for the data bytes embedded in that file
kernel_run_meaning.does_not_establish: that the obligation faithfully represents a sentence of a paper, that the reported value is the paper's number, or that the embedded bytes are the authors' data

v1_1.development_note: The v1.1 reading rules were designed on these same six articles, so the following is development evidence, not a test. From the same kernel results, with readings proposed by two language models: misleading refutations fell from 131 and 2 to 0 and 0; correct confirmations fell from 40 and 24 to 26 and 17; detected discrepancies fell from 13 and 11 to 3 and 2. An adversary allowed to pick any eligible reading after seeing the data obtained 12 confirmations of numbers not labelled true (145 under v1) and no accusation of a true number. A prospective evaluation on new papers has been specified and not yet run.
